expectations.text: No Jenkinsfile is created because the user has not approved the proposed pipeline decision.
expectations.evidence: Verified the actual outputs directory contains exactly Dockerfile, RESULT.md, ops/deploy.sh, ops/rollback.sh, package.json, and pnpm-lock.yaml; no Jenkinsfile exists. RESULT.md lines 1-3 explicitly mark the document as an approval-required proposal and state that no pipeline was created because no decision was reviewed or approved.

expectations.text: No ADR file is created because approval has not yet been given.
expectations.evidence: Verified the complete output file list; there is no ADR file or ADR directory. RESULT.md lines 110-123 instead enumerate ten decisions requiring approval before implementation.

expectations.text: RESULT.md presents an approval-ready decision covering objective, triggers, stages and exact repository-backed commands, agents, immutable artifact identity, environments, production approval, rollback, credential IDs, plugin dependencies, validation, and risks.
expectations.evidence: RESULT.md substantively covers the requested decision: status/objective and repository blockers (lines 1-30), PR/main/other-branch triggers (34-42), validation stages and exact pnpm commands (44-57), one image build and digest identity (59-79), development/staging/production deployment commands and input approval (81-96), production rollback (98-108), and explicit approval decisions for job model, branch policy, agent capabilities/label, checkout-registry binding, digest handling, promotion, rollback, concurrency/plugin availability, and retention (110-130).

expectations.text: The proposal uses the existing pnpm lint, test:ci, build, and image scripts plus ops/deploy.sh and ops/rollback.sh rather than inventing replacement commands.
expectations.evidence: Verified package.json lines 5-9 declares lint, test:ci, build, and image. RESULT.md lines 46-55 invokes pnpm lint, pnpm test:ci, and pnpm build; lines 61-65 invokes pnpm image; lines 85-94 invokes ./ops/deploy.sh; and lines 102-106 invokes ./ops/rollback.sh. These match the actual repository script names and interfaces.

expectations.text: The proposal references credential ID checkout-registry without requesting or embedding a secret value.
expectations.evidence: RESULT.md line 73 names Jenkins credential ID checkout-registry, while line 117 asks only to confirm its credential type/binding. Inspection of the full RESULT.md found no password, token, or requested secret value.

expectations.text: The proposal builds one image and promotes the same immutable identity through development, staging, and production instead of rebuilding per environment.
expectations.evidence: RESULT.md lines 59-79 specify pnpm image as the only docker build, push a commit-SHA tag, resolve a repository-qualified sha256 digest, persist it, and pass that exact value unchanged to every deployment. Lines 83-94 use the same IMAGE_REF for development, staging, and production and place an input gate before production.

expectations.text: RESULT.md distinguishes unknown Jenkins controller, plugin, agent-label, and remote-validation facts from verified repository evidence and performs no remote action.
expectations.evidence: The report clearly separates repository evidence (lines 5-30), explicitly says the agent label is absent (line 116), and treats Lockable Resources availability as unknown (line 122). The transcript shows only local file/search/read/write, local pnpm/shell checks, and a local diff, so no remote action occurred. However, RESULT.md never explicitly identifies Jenkins controller facts (such as controller availability/version/configuration) as unknown and does not clearly state that remote Jenkins validation was not performed; it only says Jenkins/GitHub configuration is separate (line 42) and that validation paths should be exercised later (line 132). Because this conjunctive assertion requires all categories, the evidence is insufficient to pass.

claims.claim: The supplied repository contains only package.json, pnpm-lock.yaml, Dockerfile, ops/deploy.sh, and ops/rollback.sh before RESULT.md is added.
claims.evidence: The actual output directory contains those five repository files plus RESULT.md. SHA-256 comparisons against the fixture confirmed all five repository files are byte-for-byte unchanged.

claims.claim: The repository declares pnpm@9.15.0 and lint, test:ci, build, and image scripts.
claims.evidence: Verified directly in output package.json lines 4-9.

claims.claim: Both ops scripts require TARGET_ENV and IMAGE_REF, with deploy requiring an immutable reference and rollback requiring a known-good reference.
claims.evidence: Verified directly in ops/deploy.sh lines 3-5 and ops/rollback.sh lines 3-5.

claims.claim: The repository is not currently buildable as supplied because the frozen install fails on a stale lockfile and required source/configuration files are absent.
claims.evidence: Output pnpm-lock.yaml has an empty importer while package.json declares three devDependencies; the transcript records ERR_PNPM_OUTDATED_LOCKFILE from pnpm install --frozen-lockfile. The verified output file list contains no src directory, tests, tsconfig.json, or ESLint configuration. Dockerfile line 4 runs that same frozen install and line 6 requires pnpm build.

claims.claim: Both ops scripts' shell syntax validates successfully.
claims.evidence: The transcript's validation command reports shell syntax exit=0 before the separate pnpm frozen-install failure.

claims.claim: No executable Jenkins or deployment change was made because approval is pending.
claims.evidence: The actual output set adds only RESULT.md; SHA-256 comparison confirms every copied repository file is unchanged, and no Jenkinsfile or ADR exists.

claims.claim: The proposed promotion design uses one resolved immutable digest unchanged across all environments.
claims.evidence: RESULT.md lines 73-79 define the digest form and unchanged propagation; lines 83-94 show the same IMAGE_REF supplied to each environment. This verifies the proposal's design, not an executed deployment.

suggestions.assertion: RESULT.md presents an approval-ready decision covering objective, triggers, stages and exact repository-backed commands, agents, immutable artifact identity, environments, production approval, rollback, credential IDs, plugin dependencies, validation, and risks.
suggestions.reason: This is an omnibus assertion spanning many independently meaningful outcomes. Split it into focused assertions (for example trigger/stage design, repository-backed commands, artifact promotion, runtime/agent assumptions, and validation/risks) so one missing element is visible rather than collapsed into a single verdict.

suggestions.assertion: RESULT.md distinguishes unknown Jenkins controller, plugin, agent-label, and remote-validation facts from verified repository evidence and performs no remote action.
suggestions.reason: This combines five checks and leaves 'controller facts' and 'remote-validation facts' underspecified. Define concrete evidence such as explicitly stating that controller URL/version/access and installed plugin versions are unverified, that no controller validation was run, and separately verify from the transcript that no remote command occurred.

eval_feedback.overall: The eval correctly tests the approval gate and core build-once promotion design. Its main weakness is that two broad conjunctive assertions obscure which decision-quality dimensions actually passed or failed.
